lead: Once the factored shear is more than the concrete can carry, the rest goes to shear reinforcement: vertical stirrups, inclined stirrups or bent-up bars. IS 456 gives one route. Find τ<sub>v</sub>, check it against τ<sub>c,max</sub>, take the concrete share τ<sub>c</sub> b d, and size the stirrups for the remainder V<sub>us</sub> from the truss formula V<sub>us</sub> = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>sv</sub> d/s<sub>v</sub>. Then check the minimum steel and the maximum spacing, and change the spacing along the span as the shear falls. Every beam on every drawing goes through this check.
prereq: You need: τv, τc, τc,max and the critical section from Behaviour of RC beams in shear.

items: At the critical section find τ<sub>v</sub> = V<sub>u</sub>/(b d) and check τ<sub>v</sub> ≤ τ<sub>c,max</sub>; if not, enlarge the section.
Read τ<sub>c</sub> for p<sub>t</sub> (bars continuing d past the section). If τ<sub>v</sub> ≤ τ<sub>c</sub>, provide minimum stirrups; otherwise V<sub>us</sub> = V<sub>u</sub> − τ<sub>c</sub> b d.
Choose the stirrup size and legs (A<sub>sv</sub> = total leg area), find s<sub>v</sub>, round it down and check the minimum steel and maximum spacing.
Find where the shear falls enough for a wider spacing, and draw the zones.

blocks.text: V<sub>us</sub> = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>sv</sub> d / s<sub>v</sub>     so     s<sub>v</sub> = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>sv</sub> d / V<sub>us</sub>
blocks.where: V<sub>us</sub> is the shear carried by vertical stirrups (N); f<sub>y</sub> is the stirrup steel strength (N/mm²) and 0.87 = 1/1.15; A<sub>sv</sub> is the total area of the stirrup legs (mm²), 2 × 50.3 = 100.5 mm² for two-legged 8 mm stirrups; d is the effective depth and s<sub>v</sub> the spacing (mm).

blocks.text: The formula is the truss analogy in one line. A 45° crack spans a length d along the beam, so it crosses d/s<sub>v</sub> stirrups, and each one yields at 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>sv</sub>. Some syllabi call τ<sub>c</sub> the 'design shear strength without shear reinforcement' and τ<sub>c,max</sub> the limit 'with shear reinforcement'. τ<sub>c,max</sub> is never subtracted from V<sub>u</sub>; only τ<sub>c</sub> b d is.
A<sub>sv</sub>/(b s<sub>v</sub>) ≥ 0.4/(0.87 f<sub>y</sub>)     so     s<sub>v</sub> ≤ 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>sv</sub>/(0.4 b)
blocks.where: b is the beam width (mm); f<sub>y</sub> is the stirrup steel strength (N/mm²), not taken greater than 415 N/mm² in this rule; the other symbols are as above.

blocks.text: Minimum stirrups are required even when τ<sub>v</sub> ≤ τ<sub>c</sub>. They hold the cage together, stop a sudden diagonal tension failure if the concrete is weaker than assumed, and give warning. IS 456 waives them only where τ<sub>v</sub> is less than half of τ<sub>c</sub> and in members of minor importance such as lintels.

Maximum spacing of vertical stirrups is the least of 0.75 d and 300 mm; for stirrups inclined at 45° it is the lesser of d and 300 mm. The idea is that every possible 45° crack must cross at least one stirrup, and in practice two.

Design aids such as SP 16 tabulate τ<sub>c</sub> against p<sub>t</sub>, and V<sub>us</sub>/d = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>sv</sub>/s<sub>v</sub> for each stirrup size and spacing. For two-legged 8 mm Fe415 stirrups at 100 mm, V<sub>us</sub>/d = 0.87 × 415 × 100.5/100 = 363 N/mm, that is 3.63 kN/cm. Divide the required V<sub>us</sub>/d into it to get the spacing directly.

sections.h3: Bent-up bars, inclined stirrups and slabs

items: Inclined stirrups or a series of bent-up bars at angle α to the beam axis: V<sub>us</sub> = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>sv</sub> d (sin α + cos α)/s<sub>v</sub>. At α = 45°, sin α + cos α = 1.414.
A single bent-up bar, or a group bent up at the same section: V<sub>us</sub> = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>sv</sub> sin α.
Bent-up bars may carry at most half of the total shear reinforcement; stirrups must carry the rest.

Solid slabs: τ<sub>c</sub> is multiplied by a factor k from 1.00 (slabs 300 mm or thicker) to 1.30 (150 mm or thinner), and τ<sub>v</sub> must not exceed half of τ<sub>c,max</sub>. Slabs are usually made thick enough to need no shear steel at all.

examples.question: Continue the beam of the previous chapter: b = 300 mm, d = 550 mm, M25, three 25 mm bars, V<sub>u</sub> = 180 kN at the critical section, τ<sub>c</sub> = 0.61 N/mm² and V<sub>us</sub> = 79.35 kN. Design two-legged 8 mm Fe415 vertical stirrups.
steps: Check the section: τ<sub>v</sub> = 1.09 N/mm² ≤ τ<sub>c,max</sub> = 3.1 N/mm². Adequate.
Maximum spacing: least of 0.75 × 550 = 412.5 mm and 300 mm, so 300 mm.
The strength value 251.5 mm governs. Round down: provide 250 mm.
Check: with s<sub>v</sub> = 250 mm, V<sub>us</sub> = 0.87 × 415 × 100.5 × 550/250 = 79.8 kN ≥ 79.35 kN. Safe.
examples.answer: Two-legged 8 mm Fe415 stirrups at 250 mm centres (strength needs 251.5 mm; minimum steel allows 302.4 mm and the code maximum is 300 mm).

examples.question: A simply supported beam with the same section (b = 300 mm, d = 550 mm, M25, three 25 mm bars running full length) has a clear span of 6 m and carries a factored load w<sub>u</sub> = 80 kN/m including self-weight. Design two-legged 8 mm Fe415 stirrups and give the spacing zones over half the span.
steps: Shear at the support face: V = 80 × 6/2 = 240 kN. At the critical section, d = 0.55 m from the face: V<sub>u</sub> = 240 − 80 × 0.55 = 196 kN.
τ<sub>v</sub> = 196 × 10³/165,000 = 1.19 N/mm² < τ<sub>c,max</sub> = 3.1 N/mm². τ<sub>c</sub> = 0.61 N/mm² as before, so the concrete carries τ<sub>c</sub> b d = 100.65 kN.
Capacity with the widest spacing allowed, 300 mm: V<sub>us</sub> = 0.87 × 415 × 100.5 × 550/300 = 66.5 kN, so the beam with stirrups at 300 mm carries 100.65 + 66.5 = 167.2 kN.
Where does the shear fall to 167.2 kN? 240 − 80 x = 167.2 gives x = 0.91 m from the face. Round up the close zone to 1.0 m.
Zone 1, from the face to 1.0 m: 8 mm stirrups at 200 mm, the first one 50 mm from the face. Zone 2, from 1.0 m to midspan: 8 mm stirrups at 300 mm (minimum steel and maximum spacing are both met).
examples.answer: Two-legged 8 mm stirrups at 200 mm for the first 1.0 m from each support face, then at 300 mm over the middle 4.0 m. The change point is where V has fallen to 167.2 kN, 0.91 m from the face.

traps: Subtracting τ<sub>c,max</sub> b d instead of τ<sub>c</sub> b d. τ<sub>c,max</sub> is only the ceiling on τ<sub>v</sub>; the concrete share is τ<sub>c</sub> b d.
Leaving V<sub>us</sub> in kN in s<sub>v</sub> = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>sv</sub> d/V<sub>us</sub>. 79.35 kN must be 79,350 N, or the spacing comes out 1000 times too large.
Taking A<sub>sv</sub> as the area of one leg. For two-legged 8 mm stirrups A<sub>sv</sub> = 100.5 mm², not 50.3 mm².
Rounding the spacing up (251.5 mm to 260 mm) or forgetting the 0.75 d and 300 mm limits. Always round down and apply all three limits.
Leaving out stirrups where τ<sub>v</sub> < τ<sub>c</sub>. Minimum shear reinforcement is still required, except where τ<sub>v</sub> < τ<sub>c</sub>/2 or in lintels.

quiz.q: State the maximum spacing of vertical stirrups in a beam.
quiz.a: The least of 0.75 d and 300 mm (for 45° inclined stirrups, the lesser of d and 300 mm).

quiz.q: Why does the stirrup formula contain d/s<sub>v</sub>?
quiz.a: An inclined crack at about 45° spans a length d along the beam, so it crosses d/s<sub>v</sub> stirrups. Each yields at 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>sv</sub>, so the total is 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>sv</sub> d/s<sub>v</sub>.

quiz.q: b = 250 mm, d = 500 mm, V<sub>u</sub> = 120 kN, τ<sub>c</sub> = 0.60 N/mm², M25. Find τ<sub>v</sub> and V<sub>us</sub>.
For that beam, find the spacing of two-legged 8 mm Fe415 stirrups.
quiz.a: Strength: s<sub>v</sub> = 0.87 × 415 × 100.5 × 500/45,000 = 403.2 mm. Minimum steel: 0.87 × 415 × 100.5/(0.4 × 250) = 362.9 mm. Maximum: least of 375 and 300 mm. Provide 300 mm.

quiz.q: One 20 mm Fe415 bar is bent up at 45°. How much shear can it carry, and can it replace all the stirrups where V<sub>us</sub> = 80 kN?
quiz.a: V<sub>us</sub> = 0.87 × 415 × 314.2 × sin 45° = 80.2 kN. No: bent-up bars may carry at most half of the shear reinforcement, so stirrups must still carry at least 40 kN.

quiz.q: In the 6 m beam of worked example 2, why can the spacing change at 1.0 m and not at 0.55 m?
quiz.a: Stirrups at 300 mm with the concrete carry only 167.2 kN. The shear is still above that until 0.91 m from the face (at 0.55 m it is 196 kN), so the close spacing must run to at least 0.91 m; 1.0 m is the practical round figure.

beyond: Not for the exam. Codes such as Eurocode 2 drop the concrete term once stirrups are needed and let the designer choose the strut angle θ between about 22° and 45°, the variable strut inclination method. Welded wire cages and headed shear studs are used in precast and in flat slabs. Search for 'variable strut inclination' and 'shear studs in flat slabs'.

figure.caption: Shear over half the 6 m span of worked example 2 against the capacity of concrete alone and of stirrups at 300 mm. The shear falls to 167.2 kN at 0.91 m, so the 200 mm zone runs to 1.0 m.
